title: terraform: private deployment: gpu node pools, iam roles, networking, and state layout refactor
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: onboarding Private deployments with GPU capacity uncovered several inconsistencies in module boundaries and state layout between environments. This PR introduces a set of Terraform modules and a state-layout refactor to standardize GPU node pools, IAM roles, and VPC networking for private (VPC/on-prem installer) deployments, plus migration helpers to avoid downtime. Key goals: 1) make GPU node-pool provisioning pluggable across cloud providers, 2) centralize IAM role templates for node and service identities, 3) enforce a repeatable VPC networking topology used by the installer and helm charts, 4) migrate per-environment local state to a predictable remote state layout for safe upgrades and rollbacks.

What this PR changes (high level): consolidated modules under modules/{gpu_node_pool, iam, network, state}; created an examples/private-deploy usage example; added scripts/migrate-state.sh that performs a guarded remote-state migration with dry-run; added acceptance tests and CI checks that run a lightweight plan against a mocked provider; updated README with migration steps and operator notes.

Checklist:
- [x] gpu_node_pool module with configurable instance types, GPU count, autoscaling parameters and taints
- [x] iam module with reusable node/service roles and least-privilege policy attachments
- [x] network module: VPC, subnets, route tables and optional private endpoints for control plane
- [x] state module: standardized remote state buckets/backends per-environment + lock configuration
- [x] migration script + operator docs
- [x] tests (unit/format/lint + acceptance plan)

Migration notes: this introduces a state-layout change that must be applied once per environment. The included scripts support a dry-run and an automated migration path; operators should schedule a maintenance window for the initial migrate to ensure consumers are quiesced. No resource recreations are expected under the documented migration steps; the script will exit with a non-zero code if any destructive plan is detected.
